This is the current six-lesson introductory study pack, not a full professional qualification. Plan about 4 active hours (240 minutes) including reading, exercises, one project and self-checking. A planning range is 180–360 minutes, depending on prior skills and revision needs. These are author estimates, not measured learner completion times.

Prerequisites: Assumes basic reading, writing and arithmetic. Use the supplied fictional case; professional use in this field still requires appropriate subject knowledge and human review.

## Suggested study sessions
- Lessons 1–3, concepts and short exercises: 60 minutes combined.
- Lesson 4, guided practical lab: 50 minutes.
- Lesson 5, error checking and correction: 30 minutes.
- Lesson 6, project, workbook and reflection: 100 minutes.
Work in manageable sessions. There is no requirement to wait a fixed number of days. Extra practice, optional videos, device setup and time waiting for teacher feedback are not part of the estimate. Record your actual time in the workbook so the teacher can improve future estimates.

## Document 4: Test and correction record
Use three rows in your notebook: normal case; missing-information case; changed or conflicting input. For each write input → expected result → observed result → pass/revise → correction. For writing or visual projects, the test can be a factual, accessibility or policy check rather than code. Keep the first attempt so the improvement is visible.

## Document 5: Self-check and teacher review rubric
Score each criterion from 0 to 4: subject accuracy; evidence and verification; practical execution; safety and appropriate permissions; clarity and independent explanation.
- 0: missing or fundamentally incorrect.
- 1: major gaps; the result cannot yet be relied on.
- 2: basic requirement met, with identified weaknesses and needed corrections.
- 3: correct and checked on the stated case; explanation is clear.
- 4: correct, independently explained and checked on a changed input; limitations are explicit.
Record a score and one evidence note per criterion, then total out of 20. The existing proposed teaching threshold is 14/20, at least 2/4 for accuracy and safety, and no unresolved serious safety issue. This is a draft review guide for teacher approval, not an automatic MELA certificate rule. A self-score is not a teacher approval.
